title: Local quasi-finiteness: representable base change, source locality and fppf target tests
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], fibred groupoids and $2$-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A morphism is representable if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Local quasi-finiteness means [pqf-def-quasifinite] on the specified scheme charts. For representable morphisms of algebraic stacks, local quasi-finiteness is preserved by arbitrary base change and composition and is local for open covers of the source: a map is locally quasi-finite if and only if its restrictions to an open cover are. If $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is representable and $q:V\to\mathcal B$ is a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space, then $f$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V\to V$ is locally quasi-finite. Flatness and local finite presentation mean [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; surjective means field-extension local lifting. Finally, for composable morphisms $A\to B\to C$ of algebraic spaces, local quasi-finiteness of $A\to C$ implies local quasi-finiteness of $A\to B$, without any hypothesis on $B\to C$.

Open-source locality follows from the etale-chart definition.

proof.text: Write $P$ for local quasi-finiteness in the scheme sense [pqf-def-quasifinite]. It is invariant under isomorphism, and local for open source covers, directly from its pointwise affine-neighbourhood definition. Identities have $P$: on an affine open the identity ring map is finite type and its fibres are one-point spectra of fields. Precomposing a map having $P$ by an etale map preserves $P$, by [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality]. In particular etale scheme maps have $P$ by applying this to an identity. Arbitrary scheme base change preserves $P$ by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change]; that clause does not assume separatedness. Composites have $P$ by [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-composition], and $P(bh)$ implies $P(h)$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-lqf-cancellation], without any assumption on $b$.

We check condition (iii) of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] for $P$. In a compatible etale scheme diagram $fa=bh$, $P(f)$ implies $P(fa)$ and hence $P(h)$ by Step 1. Conversely suppose that every $x\in X$ has the witnesses $(a:U\to X,b:V\to Y,h,u)$ in that condition, with $a(u)=x$ and $P(h)$. Since $b$ is etale, Step 1 gives $P(fa)=P(bh)$. Regard schemes as spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. By [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image], $a$ factors as a surjective etale map $U\to I$ followed by an open immersion $I\hookrightarrow X$, and $x\in I$. The scheme-test definition of an open immersion makes $I$ an open subscheme of the scheme $X$. The reverse implication of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality] gives $P(f|_I)$. Thus $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, by [pqf-def-quasifinite]; doing this for every $x$ gives $P(f)$. With (i) and (ii) from Step 1, the cited presentation criterion now applies. Consequently a space map is locally quasi-finite if and only if one compatible etale scheme presentation with surjective source chart has $P$, and then every compatible presentation has $P$. It also agrees with $P$ on schemes. We use this established criterion below.

source.place: Tags 03MJ, 03XJ, 040Z; explicit verification of etale locality using scheme Tag 03X4 and the open image of an etale map.

proof.text: For space maps $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$, choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to Z$, then a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y\times_ZW$, then $U\to X\times_YV$. These choices exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The maps $V\to Y$ and $U\to X$ are surjective etale by the base-change and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. We obtain compatible scheme maps $U\xrightarrow{h}V\xrightarrow{k}W$ presenting $f,g,gf$ simultaneously. If $f,g$ are locally quasi-finite, Step 2 gives $P(h),P(k)$; [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-composition] gives $P(kh)$, so Step 2 gives local quasi-finiteness of $gf$. If only $gf$ is locally quasi-finite, Step 2 gives $P(kh)$; [lem-sfb-scheme-lqf-cancellation] gives $P(h)$, so Step 2 gives local quasi-finiteness of $f$. No property of $g$ was used in this latter argument. This proves the final cancellation clause of the item as well as space composition.

source.place: Tag 03XK, lemma-composition-quasi-finite; Tag 03XN, lemma-permanence-quasi-finite; compatible presentations as in Tag 02X1.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a locally quasi-finite space map and let $Y\prime\to Y$ be arbitrary. Choose a scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a scheme atlas $U\to X\times_YV$, both surjective etale, so $P(U\to V)$ by Step 2. Choose also a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\prime\to Y\prime\times_YV$. All these spaces and atlases exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The scheme $U\prime=U\times_VV\prime$ has a surjective etale map to $X\times_YY\prime$: first its map to $X\times_YV\prime$ is the base change of $U\to X\times_YV$, and then $X\times_YV\prime\to X\times_YY\prime$ is the base change of $V\prime\to Y\prime$. Their properties follow from [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; the same node makes $V\prime\to Y\prime$ surjective etale. The scheme map $U\prime\to V\prime$ is the base change of $U\to V$, so it has $P$ by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change]. Step 2 applied to this presentation proves local quasi-finiteness of $X\times_YY\prime\to Y\prime$.

source.place: Tags 03XL, lemma-base-change-quasi-finite, and 0ABM, lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus, atlas proof.

proof.text: For a space map $f:X\to Y$ and an open cover $(X_i)$ of $X$, fix a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X\times_YV$. Pulling back the opens gives open subschemes $U_i$ covering $U$. The meaning of open cover is the scheme-test meaning in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], and the atlases and their pullbacks use [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Each $U_i\to X_i$ is an etale scheme chart by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. If every $f|_{X_i}$ is locally quasi-finite, Step 2 gives $P(U_i\to V)$ for each $i$. For each $u\in U$, choose $i$ with $u\in U_i$; the affine-neighbourhood witnesses for $U_i\to V$ at $u$ are also witnesses for $U\to V$. Thus $P(U\to V)$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite], and Step 2 gives local quasi-finiteness of $f$. Conversely any compatible presentation of $f|_{X_i}$ is one of $f$, because an open inclusion is etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]); hence all such presentations have $P$. This proves both directions of open source locality, also for the empty cover of an empty source.

source.place: Tag 03XJ, definition-locally-quasi-finite; Tag 040Z and pointwise scheme definition Tag 01TD.

proof.text: We next prove the scheme-target descent calculation needed below. Let $Z\to T$ be a space map with $T$ a scheme, and let $u:D\to T$ be a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map. Suppose $Z_D\to D$ is locally quasi-finite. The singleton $\{u\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site], and therefore an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]; this does not assume $u$ quasi-compact. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $E\to Z$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its base change $E_D\to Z_D$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; $E_D=E\times_TD$ is a scheme. Step 2 gives $P(E_D\to D)$ using target chart $\operatorname{id}_D$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-lqf-fpqc-descent] to $E\to T$ and the covering $\{u\}$ to obtain $P(E\to T)$. Step 2 with charts $E\to Z$ and $\operatorname{id}_T$ gives local quasi-finiteness of $Z\to T$.

source.place: spaces-descent.tex Tag 0427, lemma-descending-property-quasi-finite, scheme-atlas reduction; descent.tex Tag 02VI.

proof.text: For a representable stack map $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, its definition tests local quasi-finiteness on every scheme base change. The same test is valid with any algebraic space $H\to\mathcal B$. Indeed $A_H=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}H$ is an algebraic space by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space]. Choose surjective etale scheme atlases $D\to H$ and $E\to A_H\times_HD$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The map $E\to A_H$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The map $A_H\times_HD\to D$ identifies with the scheme test $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}D\to D$, using the triple definition of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. It is locally quasi-finite, so Step 2 gives $P(E\to D)$. Step 2 again, now for the compatible presentation $E\to D$ of $A_H\to H$, gives local quasi-finiteness of that map. Conversely the algebraic-space tests include all scheme tests, since schemes are spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. For space maps themselves this scheme-test interpretation agrees with the chart property: one direction is Step 4, and the other uses one surjective etale scheme target atlas and Step 2.

source.place: stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XC, lemma-property-spaces-too, specialized to local quasi-finiteness.

proof.text: Representability is preserved by arbitrary $2$-base change and composition by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], and the required base changes of algebraic stacks exist by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. For an arbitrary $\mathcal B\prime\to\mathcal B$, the test of $f\prime:\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B\prime\to\mathcal B\prime$ at a scheme $T\to\mathcal B\prime$ is $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T\to T$: on triples forget the redundant $\mathcal B\prime$-object identified with the given one from $T$, and conversely insert it and its identity. These inverse operations on objects and arrows are the $2$-fibre-product definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Hence local quasi-finiteness of $f$ proves that of every $f\prime$.

source.place: Representable scheme-test definition in stacks-properties.tex Section 04XB; associativity of 2-fibre products.

proof.text: For representable locally quasi-finite maps $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal C$ and a scheme $T\to\mathcal C$, put $B_T=\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}T$ and $A_T=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}T$. Both are spaces by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space], representability of the composite having been established in Step 8. The map $B_T\to T$ is locally quasi-finite by the test for $g$, and $A_T\to B_T$ is so by Step 7 applied to $f$ and $B_T\to\mathcal B$. Step 3 gives local quasi-finiteness of $A_T\to T$. This holds for every $T$, proving stack composition. For an open cover of the source of a representable map, every scheme base change carries the pulled-back open cover. The definition of open cover in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] says exactly that these opens cover the space on scheme charts. Apply Step 5 to each test. It proves both directions of open source locality for the stack map.

source.place: Space composition Tag 03XK transferred by scheme tests; open source locality of the chart definition.

proof.text: Finally let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be representable and let $q:V\to\mathcal B$ be representable, surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, with $V$ an algebraic space, and put $A_V=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V$. The forward implication is Step 7. For the converse assume $A_V\to V$ locally quasi-finite and fix any scheme $t:T\to\mathcal B$. Put $Z=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T$, $H=V\times_{\mathcal B}T$, spaces by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space]. The map $H\to T$ is surjective flat locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $D\to H$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The same calculus makes $u:D\to H\to T$ surjective flat locally finitely presented. Let $v:D\to V$ be the other map and $\beta:qv\xrightarrow{\sim}tu$ its specified isomorphism. There is an isomorphism over $D$, $Z\times_TD\simeq A_V\times_VD$: send an object $(a,d,\alpha:f(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}t(u(d)))$ to $(a,v(d),\beta(d)^{-1}\alpha,d)$, and invert this by composing with $\beta(d)$. These inverse operations preserve arrows and pullback, by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Step 4 makes the right side locally quasi-finite over $D$, as a base change of $A_V\to V$. Step 6 descends through $u$ and gives local quasi-finiteness of $Z\to T$. Since $t$ was arbitrary this is local quasi-finiteness of $f$. The covering used is $H\to T$, not $Z\times_TH\to T$, so no surjectivity of $f$ is presumed.
